name: David R. Pelizzon
current_role: President, Squadron Capital LLC (Granby, CT); director of OrthoPediatrics Corp. (KIDS) and Alphatec Holdings (ATEC)
profile: Retired U.S. Army colonel turned private-equity investor who founded/runs Squadron Capital, a firm making direct investments in operating companies, chiefly orthopedic and spine medtech. Squadron is a 10%+ holder of OrthoPediatrics (board seat since 2011) and a major Alphatec holder (board seat since 2020).
interesting_fact: He served almost 30 years on active duty in U.S. Army airborne and special operations units before retiring in 2003 and moving into manufacturing and investing.
deep_cut_fact: A West Point graduate with advanced degrees from Harvard and the U.S. Naval War College, he spent his first post-Army years as a manufacturing executive in the U.S. and Asia.

name: Christopher R. Christensen
current_role: Co-founder and former Executive Chairman of The Ensign Group (retired Sept 1, 2025); director of The Pennant Group (PNTG) since 2019
profile: Co-founded skilled-nursing and post-acute operator The Ensign Group with his father Roy in 1999, served as president from inception, took it public as CEO in 2006, and became executive chairman in 2019. He also co-founded CareTrust REIT and The Pennant Group. He retired from Ensign's board and executive chair role on Sept 1, 2025, staying on as an 'ambassador' for the company.
interesting_fact: Ensign is famous for its decentralized model: Christensen credits the company's 'collective distrust in a traditional, top-down corporate model', giving local facility leaders CEO-like autonomy, for its growth to 340+ facilities.
deep_cut_fact: A BYU economics graduate, he has chaired BYU's President's Leadership Council and sat on the Marriott School's National Advisory Council, and has done missionary and humanitarian work in Guatemala, the Dominican Republic and Ghana.
notes: Now retired from Ensign, so the Ensign IR inbox is an indirect route; he also sits on the board of Behavioral Health Solutions (bhs.health) and remains linked to Pennant. Ensign's leaders are known as private 'quiet men' (OCBJ).

name: Iqbal Ahmed
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive, Seamark Group (Manchester seafood processor/exporter)
profile: Bangladesh-born British entrepreneur (b. 1956, Sylhet) who moved to the UK at 15, joined his family's Oldham business and, with brothers Kamal and Bilal, built Seamark/Ibco into a major frozen-seafood importer, processor and catering supplier with a processing plant in Chittagong. The family also has interests in hotels, property and hospitality in Manchester.
interesting_fact: Known in the British-Bangladeshi community as 'Mr Shrimp' or 'King Prawn'; his brands include Mr Prawn, Lily, Classic and Tiger, and he was made an OBE in 2001 for services to international trade.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 George Osborne invited him onto the New Enterprise Council think tank, and in 2012 he won the international category of EY's North region Entrepreneur of the Year awards.
notes: Family business; profile largely from older UK press. Seamark site did not return a contact page when checked. Wealth is family-held (brothers Kamal and Bilal).

name: Aart J. de Geus
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chair, Synopsys Inc. (SNPS); director, Applied Materials (AMAT)
profile: Dutch-born electrical engineer (b. 1954) and a pioneer of logic synthesis / electronic design automation, who co-founded Synopsys in 1986 out of GE and led it as CEO until January 2024, building the leading chip-design software company (including the Ansys acquisition). He now serves as executive chair, alongside board roles at Applied Materials and industry groups.
interesting_fact: He is lead guitarist of the Silicon Valley blues band 'Legally Blue', and speaks English, German, Swiss-German, French and Dutch.
deep_cut_fact: At GE he led the team behind SOCRATES, a rule-based logic-synthesis expert system, finishing his SMU PhD at night; when GE exited semiconductors he persuaded GE vice chair Ed Hood to back a spin-off with $400,000 for equity, which became Synopsys.
notes: Highly relevant to AI/data-center chip design theme; gives a long Computer History Museum oral history (2009). Route via Synopsys corporate PR.

name: Pradeep Sindhu
current_role: Co-founder of Juniper Networks; founder of data-center chip company Fungible (acquired by Microsoft in 2023); current title not verified
profile: Indian-American computer scientist (b. 1953, Varanasi; IIT Kanpur, Univ. of Hawaii, CMU PhD) who spent 11 years at Xerox PARC before co-founding Juniper Networks in 1996, where he architected the M40 router and served as CEO then chief scientist. He later founded Fungible, maker of data processing units (DPUs) for data centers, which Microsoft acquired.
interesting_fact: He architected Juniper's first product, the M40 core internet router, which helped Juniper challenge Cisco in backbone routing after its 1999 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: At Xerox PARC he worked on VLSI design tools and high-speed shared-memory multiprocessor interconnects; that work influenced the architecture of Sun Microsystems' SPARCcenter 2000 and SPARCserver 1000 systems.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center theme (DPUs, networking). Web search budget ran out before his post-Fungible role at Microsoft and any published contact could be verified; re-check his current title before outreach.

name: Vikram Indrajit Shah
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Shalby Ltd (Shalby Hospitals), Ahmedabad
profile: Ahmedabad orthopaedic surgeon (b. 1962) who trained in joint replacement in the UK (Wrightington/Ormskirk), Switzerland, Germany and the US, then founded Shalby in 1994 as a six-bed knee-replacement unit. It grew into a listed multispecialty hospital chain with 2,000+ beds and over 100,000 joint replacements performed.
interesting_fact: He set a record of 3,000 knee replacement surgeries at a single centre in 2008, and his 'Zero Technique' cut total knee replacement time to roughly 7-12 minutes.
deep_cut_fact: He invented the 'OS Needle' (Orthopaedic Surgeons' Needle), able to pass through both bone and soft tissue, for which he received an award from Johnson & Johnson; he was also the only Indian surgeon on Zimmer's Board of Designers.
notes: His personal site drvikramshah.com routes to info@shalby.org. Note Shalby's Wikipedia page is tagged as promotional; surgery-count claims are company-sourced.

name: Stanley M. Bergman
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Henry Schein Inc. (HSIC); stepped down as CEO at end of 2025 (successor: Frederick Lowery)
profile: South African-born accountant who joined dental and medical supplies distributor Henry Schein in 1980, became CFO and then CEO in 1989, and led it through its 1995 Nasdaq IPO and roughly 200 acquisitions into a global healthcare distributor. He handed the CEO role to Frederick Lowery (ex-Thermo Fisher) and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He ran Henry Schein as CEO for about 36 years (1989-2025), one of the longest CEO tenures in the S&P 500, and was Chief Executive magazine's 2017 CEO of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: He arrived in New York from South Africa in 1976 and worked as an accountant before joining Henry Schein in 1980; his 'doing well by doing good' approach became the subject of a Harvard Business School case study.
notes: Known for public-private health partnerships and corporate social responsibility work. Web search budget ran out before Henry Schein's media/IR email could be verified; check the contact block of a recent Henry Schein press release.
